_about: Public-domain Franciscus Junius the elder (Francois du Jon, 1545-1602), Reformed professor at Heidelberg and Leiden, for the Word Hoard: his commentary on the Revelation in English (London: Richard Field, catalogued 1592; and the new translation, Cambridge: John Legat, 1596, dedication signed T. B.) and A Christian Letter of admonition against separation from the church assemblies in England (catalogued 1602), from Internet Archive scans of Early English Books. Not the younger Junius, the philologist. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 39 (a pickup: the 2026-10-23 closing note that no English Junius was on the Archive was wrong, and is corrected here); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

junius-apocalypsis-1592: Apocalypsis: A briefe and learned commentarie upon the Revelation of S. Iohn, written in Latine by M. Francis Du Jon (Imprinted at London by Richard Field; catalogued 1592)
junius-apocalyps-1596: The Apocalyps, or Revelation of S. Iohn, with a briefe and methodicall exposition, set forth by Fr. Du Ion, newly translated (Cambridge: Iohn Legat, 1596)
junius-christian-letter-1602: A Christian Letter, containing a grave and godly admonition to such as make separation from the Church assemblies in England, by Master Francis Iunius, Divinitie Reader at Leyden (for Robert Dexter; catalogued 1602)

_alternates.junius-letters-1602: Certayne Letters (1602), two by Junius and one by the exiled English church at Amsterdam, tr. R. G.: mixed authorship

_excluded.junius-other: His Latin works (Defensio, De Politiae Mosis, Lectiones in Ionam, De Theologia Vera); the 1599 Geneva-Tomson Bible; the younger Junius's Painting of the Ancients (a different man)

_identity_checked.junius-apocalyps-1596: title page read from the page image: 'Lately set forth by Fr. Du Ion, and newly translated into English', Printed by John Legat, Printer to the Universitie of Cambridge, 1596; the dedication to John Boyse is signed T. B. (the OCR misses the name)
